summary: Dependency resolved from unpinned GitHub branch enables install-time code execution
details: The package.json of @chatest/baileys@4.4.0 declares the `libsignal` dependency as `github:chatunitycenter/libsignal-node` with no commit SHA, tag, or semver pin. On `npm install`, this resolves to whatever bytes are at the default branch HEAD of that external GitHub repository at the moment of installation, including any lifecycle scripts contained in them. The dependency is actively consumed via `require("libsignal")` in `lib/Signal/libsignal.js`, so it is part of the runtime tree and loaded on module import as well. Whoever controls the referenced GitHub repository controls code that runs on every installer's machine, unpinned and integrity-unchecked. The package also exhibits a scope/branding mismatch: it is published as `@chatest/baileys` but its `homepage` and `repository.url` both point at `@chatunity/baileys`, and the README banner brands the module as `ChatUnity Baileys`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
